children: Chicago soybean futures edged lower on Friday after notching life-of-contract highs in the last session amid China's purchase of U.S. beans before the upcoming meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping. Wheat and corn also dropped.
FUNDAMENTALS
* The most-traded soybeans on the Chicago Board of Trade
fell 0.6% to $13.24-3/4 a bushel by 0145 GMT. CBOT wheat
dropped 0.9% at $7.34-3/4 a bushel, while corn
lost 0.8% to $5.29-1/4 a bushel. Soybeans gained 1.2%, wheat rose 0.14% and corn 1.3% so far this week.
* Soybean futures jumped to their highest point in three-year supported by Chinese demand in the last session.

* China has bought around 1 million metric tons of U.S. soybeans this week, traders told Reuters, as the world's top oilseed buyer steps up purchases ahead of Chinese President Xi Jinping's visit to Washington later this month.
* The purchases take China's total U.S. soybean buying to nearly half of the 25 million tons the White House said Beijing had committed to annually through 2028.
* The USDA confirmed additional Chinese purchases of U.S. soybeans on Wednesday and Thursday.
* Positioning ahead of Friday's U.S. Department of Agriculture supply and demand report helped drive soybean futures higher.
* The USDA's supply-and-demand forecasts on Friday are expected to indicate the extent to which hot, dry spells this summer hurt U.S. Midwest crops.
* Brazil's soy exports are seen reaching 7.74 million metric tons in September versus 6.97 million tons in the same period last year, according to grain exporters union ANEC.
MARKET NEWS

* Oil prices rose on Friday and both major benchmarks are on track to end the week at over $100 a barrel for the first time since mid-May, as increasing attacks along key shipping routes in the Middle East fuel fears of a prolonged disruption to supplies.
